newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: S. Leone catches illegal aliens digging diamonds.
newsitem.headline: S. Leone catches illegal aliens digging diamonds.

text.p: Police in Sierra Leone have arrested 67 foreigners in the eastern diamond town of Koidu on charges of entering the West African country illegally and digging for diamonds, police sources said on Friday.
Those detained included Gambians, Lebanese, Guineans, Malians, Nigerians, one Russian and one Senegalese, they said, adding that the crackdown would continue.

An attack on the town last year by rebels who took up arms in 1991 killed more than 200 people. The sources say that hundreds of illegal immigrants have since flocked back to the town, making security a problem there.
Most crossed into Sierra Leone from neighbouring Guinea, they added.
Koidu is a major contributor to the impoverished nation's foreign exchange earnings. Foreigners in Sierra Leone legally need special licences to mine or export diamonds.

Sierra Leonians from elsewhere in the country need residence permits to stay and work in Koidu, which is protected by private South African security firm Executive Outcomes. The firm has fought with the army against the rebels.
Illegal immigrants caught mining illegally risk confiscation of their assets, heavy fines or jail and deportation.

A fragile truce holds but peace talks between the civilian government, which took office in March, and the rebels are stalled on differences over withdrawal of foreign forces, including Executive Outcomes.
